name: Fan API: your account (/v1/me)
description: The signed-in user's own tickets (with the live rotating barcode), orders, transfers, memberships, season passes and flex packs, refund requests, wallet passes, tokens and profile, for fan apps and assistants. Authenticate with a user token holding me:read / me:write: a personal access token (Profile → Developer), an account token (a user with no organization, or minted by another of your tokens) or an OAuth token an app got with your consent. An organization API key has no user and is refused. Every call runs as you through the app's own rules (transfer locks, claim keys, refund windows), and nothing here ever answers another user's data or a barcode secret.

endpoints.description: Sends tickets of one of your orders to someone by email: by default every ticket of it you can transfer, or the ticket_ids you name (they must be the order's). Each ticket is locked while the transfer is pending (no barcode, no second transfer, no wallet pass), exactly as in the app; the receiver claims it with the link mailed to them, and you can cancel until then. Answers each transfer and its claim_key (the link's key, for sharing it yourself). Opendate POST /orders/{order_id}/ticket_transfers.

endpoints.summary: Ask for a refund of an order
endpoints.description: Asks the organizer to refund tickets of one of your orders: by default those you still hold, or the ticket_ids you name. The event's refund policy and window decide (each ticket answers ok, or a reason: closed, all-sales-final, not-buyer, …); a ticket with an open request answers existing. The organizer refunds or declines; the money goes back to how it was paid. Opendate POST /public/orders/{order_id}/refund_request.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: At most 500 characters (Opendate's notes is accepted too).

endpoints.description: Mints a token for yourself (Opendate POST /personal_access_tokens). A personal access token makes a personal token for the same organization (your role's rules apply); an account token makes an account token (me:read / me:write only). The new token gets at most the scopes of the token that makes it and never outlives it. It always expires (30, 90 or 365 days), is revoked with the token that made it, and can't mint tokens itself (make those in Profile → Developer). It is shown once. Needs a personal access token or an account token: an OAuth app never manages its user's tokens.

parameters.name: expires_days
parameters.description: 30, 90 (default) or 365, cut to your token's own expiry. Never null: a minted token always expires.
